why: Facts from the raw log: (1) neither version returned a single 5xx and the only status code in the whole run is 200. (2) Over the full 120 s the canary's aggregate p95 is 177 ms vs 94 ms for stable, which is what the dashboard flags. (3) That gap is confined to the start of the run: p95 in 0-30 s is 210 ms canary vs 93 ms stable and in 30-60 s is 130 ms canary vs 94 ms stable. (4) From t=60 s on the two versions are indistinguishable: canary n=1261 p50=36 p95=94 p99=104 vs stable n=3651 p50=34 p95=95 p99=104. (5) The same steady-state parity holds per route after 60 s: /browse p95 27 vs 27, /search 59 vs 59, /checkout 103 vs 104. (6) The last two windows confirm it is flat, not drifting: 60-90 s p95 95 canary / 95 stable and 90-120 s p95 94 canary / 94 stable. JUDGEMENT: the elevated aggregate p95 is a one-time warm-up transient of the single fresh canary pod (cold caches / JIT / connection pool fill) that decays monotonically 210 -> 130 -> 95 -> 94 ms and is over within the first minute; it is not a regression, since the steady state matches stable on every route at p50/p95/p99 with zero errors. A 120 s test is short and only ~25% of traffic hit one pod, so JUDGEMENT: promote, but watch p95 and 5xx during the ramp to 100% and keep the rollback ready, because warm-up cost will briefly recur on each newly started pod.

claims.claim: Neither version returned any 5xx; the only HTTP status present in the whole run is 200.
Over the full 120 s run the canary aggregate p95 is 177 ms (n=2476) versus 94 ms for stable (n=7343).
claims.query:
const P=(rs,f)=>pct(rs.map(r=>r.ms),f);
print('FULLRUN canary n='+canary.length+' p95='+P(canary,0.95)+' | stable n='+stable.length+' p95='+P(stable,0.95));
claims.expect: FULLRUN canary n=2476 p95=177 | stable n=7343 p95=94

claims.claim: The canary's latency penalty is concentrated in the first 60 s: p95 210 ms vs stable 93 ms in 0-30 s, and 130 ms vs 94 ms in 30-60 s.
After t=60 s the canary matches stable on every percentile: canary n=1261 p50=36 p95=94 p99=104 versus stable n=3651 p50=34 p95=95 p99=104.
Per-route steady state after 60 s is at parity: /browse p95 27 ms canary vs 27 ms stable, /search 59 vs 59, /checkout 103 vs 104.
The last two windows are flat rather than degrading: 60-90 s p95 95 ms canary vs 95 ms stable, and 90 s to end p95 94 ms canary vs 94 ms stable.
